paragraphs.text: Or, “no darkness at all in him.”

“You may . . . commit a sin.” Gr., ha·marʹte·te, a verb in the aorist subjunctive. According to A Grammar of New Testament Greek, by James H. Moulton, Vol. I, 1908, p. 109, “the Aorist has a ‘punctiliar’ action, that is, it regards action as a point: it represents the point of entrance . . . or that of completion . . . or it looks at a whole action simply as having occurred, without distinguishing any steps in its progress.”
Lit., “propitiation.” Lat., pro·pi·ti·aʹti·o. See Heb 9:5 ftn.
“Antichrist.” Gr., an·tiʹkhri·stos; Lat., an·ti·chriʹstus; J17(Heb.), tsar ham·ma·shiʹach.
“The Devil.” Gr., tou Di·a·boʹlou; Lat., Di·aʹbo·lo; J17,18,22(Heb.), has·Sa·tanʹ.
“From [the] beginning.” Gr., apʼ ar·khesʹ; Lat., ab i·niʹti·o; J17(Heb.), me·roʼshʹ.
Or, “life.” Gr., psy·khenʹ; Lat., aʹni·mam; J17,18,22(Heb.), naph·shohʹ, “his soul.” See App 4A.
“Inspired expression.” Lit., “spirit.” Gr., pneuʹma·ti; Lat., spi·riʹtu·i; J17,18,22(Heb.), ruʹach.
Or, “test the spirits.” Lit., “be you proving the spirits.”
Or, “checking; correction; punishment.” Lit., “lopping off.” Gr., koʹla·sin. Compare Mt 25:46 where the same Gr. word occurs.
“Is bearing witness.” Gr., mar·ty·rounʹ; Lat., te·sti·fi·caʹtur.

After “witness bearers” אABVgSyh,p omit the words added in later Gr. mss and Vgc, namely: “in heaven, the Father, the Word and the holy spirit; and these three are one. (8) And there are three witness bearers on earth.”
Lit., “the three [witness bearers] are into the one (thing).” Compare Joh 10:30 ftn. For a discussion of this vs, see App 6B.
Or, “this is the freeness of speech.”
That is, God, according to context.
“The One born from God,” that is, Jesus Christ the Son of God, as in vs 1; א, “the one born from God (keeps himself)”; Vg, “the generation of God (keeps him).”
